messages:

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: short-term remote pay subsidy model for APAC hires (SG/IN exceptions)

Hi Laura + Marcus —

Quick summary: we have an inbound candidate (Mei Chen via Sunrise Talent) who is a high-likelihood hire for Backend Lead but expects S$180k. Our US band for the role is $170k (base) and the APAC guideline would land at ~S$150k after localization. Recruiting recommends bridging to close the offer; the hiring manager recommends a short-term pay subsidy to match S$170k for first 12 months while we finalize localized bands and comp approvals.

Request: please review the attached toy model (col-subsidy-model.xlsx) and tell me if we can: 1) approve a 12-month subsidy for SG hires when candidate merits and retention risk justify it, and 2) if so, define the accounting & approval path (finance offset? one-off sign-on vs monthly subsidy?).

Notes:
- This is intended as an interim policy (90–365 days) while we finish the regional comp calibration project.
- We should limit headcount-wide exceptions; prefer a documented memo + manager sign-off.

I know finance + comp will need to weigh in; looping Stephanie here for initial comp guidance.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
TA/Recruiting Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: col-subsidy-model.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposal: short-term remote pay subsidy model for APAC hires (SG/IN exceptions)

Thanks Rachel — good context. A few initial thoughts:

- I support a narrowly-scoped, time-bound subsidy for high-impact hires where market delta is >10% and candidate/manager risk of walking is high. This matches precedent we've used for SF->LA transitions historically.
- Important to separate subsidy (company-funded temporary top-up) from permanent base increases. For budgeting, Finance wants the subsidy captured as a recruiting/people expense and amortized over expected tenure for forecasting.
- Approvals: hiring manager + TA lead + finance partner (Marcus) should be sufficient for an allocation up to S$30k uplift; anything >S$30k requires People Head sign-off.

Can Marcus confirm finance treatment and whether we need a PO or special ledger code?

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations

Subject: Re: Proposal: short-term remote pay subsidy model for APAC hires (SG/IN exceptions)

Thanks — quick finance notes:

- We can treat the subsidy as a recruiting expense (non-headcount recurring comp) and tag it to a temporary P&L code. For offers paid as a lump (sign-on) it's cleaner from payroll, but amortizing monthly as a stipend is fine and makes churn behavior observable.
- For Singapore specifically: our payroll vendor needs a one-off memo to process monthly stipend starting in the first payroll cycle. That memo should live in the employee file (SG regulation).
- Thresholds: Marcus concurs with Laura: up to S$30k uplift can be approved by manager + TA + finance partner. >S$30k escalates to People Head and CFO notification.

I'll draft a short exception memo if you want — also can speak to tax withholding implications (small for stipend, bigger for lump sign-on).

Marcus
Finance Business Partner

Appreciate the details. A couple comp-practical points:

- The localization project is ~60% complete; band recommendations for SG/IN expected in Q1 2027. Until then we need a repeatable exception path.
- Suggested rules for the subsidy pilot:
  * Eligibility: senior ICs and managers only (L4+), critical skills (backend infra, model serving, SRE).
  * Cap: subsidy should not exceed 15% of published US band for the role in first 12 months (except by explicit People Head approval).
  * Documentation: manager justification + signed subsidy memo attached to offer letter.

- For the Mei Chen case: she checks the boxes (senior backend lead, high leverage). S$170k for first 12 months via monthly stipend is reasonable; then re-evaluate at performance review for permanent band alignment.

I'll prepare sample language for the offer letter and the subsidy memo.

—Stephanie
Compensation Manager
